newsitem.title: GERMANY: German GOVT coalition will stay together, says FDP.
newsitem.headline: German GOVT coalition will stay together, says FDP.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition government will smooth over cracks in the alliance of Christian Democrats (CDU) and Free Democrats (FDP) and will continue through to the next election, leading FDP officials said on Monday.

FDP chairman Wolfgang Gerhardt told reporters after a meeting of the party's leadership that an agreement with Kohl's CDU on new budget savings measures without tax increases in 1997 and 1998 was becoming apparent.
"The coalition will stick together," said Gerhardt.
He said a savings package could include further privatisations and a supplementary 1997 federal budget.

Hermann Otto Solms, leader of the FDP parliamentary group, sought to dispel fears that the coalition could fall apart over a dispute about possible tax increases and dismissed opposition hopes that the elections could be brought forward.
"There is no reason for concern or hope," he said, adding that the coalition had a voter mandate to govern until the next general election in September 1998.
Neither Gerhardt nor Solms would be drawn on the FDP's detailed budget proposals.
